items.q: What does Pocock call the most valuable skill with AI?
items.a: **Communication**: telling agents what you care about, because the human-to-agent gap **never closes on its own**.

items.q: What should you be aware of when designing with agents?
items.a: Your **unknown unknowns** such as security and deployment; otherwise the agent **just makes stuff up**.
One **shared vocabulary** used the same way by client, code, database and UI, so the agent builds **what you actually mean**.

items.q: Why did spec-driven development fail for him?
items.a: The code kept getting worse; **code is the agent's environment**, so a messy codebase means **garbage in, garbage out**.

items.q: What effort level does he run Opus 5.5 at?
items.a: **Medium**, maybe lower: strong tests mean the agent **doesn't need to work as hard**, and it's faster and cheaper.

items.q: How should a beginner start with agents?
items.a: **Climb the trust ladder**: learn the brake first, **watch the agent like a hawk**, then add agents, skills and data sources.

items.q: What tasks should you give AI first?
items.a: Your **boring, checkable work** (draft replies, first drafts), not your most ambitious goal.

items.q: Where is the big AI career opportunity?
items.a: Turning **knowledge-work processes into agent workflows** for organizations, which is hard because real work is **hard to verify**.
